newsitem.title: USA: De Silguy sees close watch on ERM fx rates.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy sees close watch on ERM fx rates.

text.p: The sustainability of exchange rates in Europe's new exchange rate mechanism to be launched after monetary union will be the subject of continuous surveillance, European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Sunday.
The ERM II will link currencies of countries not yet ready to join monetary union with the euro after it is launched in 1999.

"In order to avoid speculation, the sustainability of central rates will be the subject of continuous surveillance and the realignment of central rates -- when necessary -- will be effected in a timely manner," de Silguy said, according to an advance copy of a speech prepared for delivery to the International Monetary Fund's Interim Committee on Sunday.
"Intervention will remain an important feature of the new mechanism, but the emphasis will be on sound macroeconomic management as the means to provide exchange rate stability," he added.

"In this context, we see a strong link between the sustainability of exchange rates and the convergence efforts of the non-participant member states towards the standard of stability set by the euro area," he added.

In the ERM II, endorsed by European Union finance ministers in Dublin last weekend, currencies will be allowed to fluctuate in wide bands, similar to the 15 percent bands of the existing exchange rate mechanism.
The wide standard fluctuation bands will not exclude narrower bands for some currencies whose monetary and fiscal performances are closer to those in the euro zone, de Silguy said.
